title: Written register and negation: である, でもある, となっている, ず／ずに, なし and ことか

constructions.label: である: plain written copula, also inside a clause before こと
でもある: is also (an added identity or quality)
でもない: is not … either
となっている as a rule or fixed arrangement in effect (決まり)
となっている as a state reached through change (変化)
Verb stem (連用形) linking clauses in writing: the action happens
ず linking clauses in writing: the action does not happen
なしでは + negative: X is needed (必要)
なしでも／なしで: X is not needed (不要)
ことか: exclaiming how great a degree is (強調)
Embedded question with か: an amount is asked about (質問)

relationships.label: Copula style: plain written である or polite です
Add an identity with でもある, or deny one more with でもない
Read となっている as a rule in effect or as a result of change
Written clause link: verb stem or ず
Without doing: written ずに or everyday ないで
Read なし: is the item needed or not?
Exclamation with ことか or an embedded question with か

exercises.prompt:
【報告】事故は午後三時ごろに起きた。
原因は機械の故障____。
exercises.translation: Insert only である or です. A copula at the end of a sentence keeps the style (plain or polite) of the text around it. Inside a clause, use the form that is grammatical in that position. The text inside 【】 names the kind of text.
exercises.evidence: The report's other sentence ends in plain 起きた, so the copula stays plain.
exercises.explanation: Report: The accident happened at around 3 p.m. The cause was a machine fault. The report is written in plain style (起きた), so the plain written copula である keeps the style consistent.

options.label: である
options.rationale: Report: The accident happened at around 3 p.m. The cause was a machine fault. The report is written in plain style (起きた), so the plain written copula である keeps the style consistent.

options.label: です
options.rationale: です does not fit this context: the report's other sentence ends in plain 起きた, and the instruction asks for the style of the surrounding text, so a polite ending would mix styles.

exercises.prompt:

exercises.translation: Insert only である or です. A copula at the end of a sentence keeps the style (plain or polite) of the text around it. Inside a clause, use the form that is grammatical in that position. The text inside 【】 names the kind of text.
exercises.evidence: The essay's next sentence ends in plain ためている, so the copula stays plain.
exercises.explanation: Essay: My dream is to travel all over the world. For that, I am saving money every month. The essay continues in plain style (ためている), so である keeps the style consistent.

options.label: である
options.rationale: Essay: My dream is to travel all over the world. For that, I am saving money every month. The essay continues in plain style (ためている), so である keeps the style consistent.

options.label: です
options.rationale: です does not fit this context: the essay's next sentence ends in plain ためている, and the instruction asks for the style of the surrounding text, so a polite ending would mix styles.

exercises.prompt: この建物が市で一番古い学校____ことは、あまり知られていません。
exercises.translation: Insert only である or です. A copula at the end of a sentence keeps the style (plain or polite) of the text around it. Inside a clause, use the form that is grammatical in that position. The text inside 【】 names the kind of text.
exercises.evidence: The blank is inside a clause that modifies こと, not at the end of the sentence.
exercises.explanation: It is not widely known that this building is the oldest school in the city. The copula sits inside the clause before こと, where a noun needs a form that can modify a following noun: である can (学校であること). The polite style of the whole sentence is carried by 知られていません at the end.

options.label: である
options.rationale: It is not widely known that this building is the oldest school in the city. The copula sits inside the clause before こと, where a noun needs a form that can modify a following noun: である can (学校であること). The polite style of the whole sentence is carried by 知られていません at the end.

options.label: です
options.rationale: です does not fit this slot: the blank is inside the clause before こと, and です does not attach before こと here (学校ですこと is not a well-formed noun clause); the sentence's politeness is already carried by 知られていません.

exercises.explanation: Notice: The library is closed every Monday. Please take note. The notice addresses readers politely (ご注意ください), so the polite copula です keeps the style consistent.

options.label: です
options.rationale: Notice: The library is closed every Monday. Please take note. The notice addresses readers politely (ご注意ください), so the polite copula です keeps the style consistent.

exercises.prompt:
父は医者であり、小説家____。
休みの日には家で小説を書いている。
exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The next line says he writes novels, so 小説家 is a second identity he has.
exercises.explanation: My father is a doctor and also a novelist. On his days off he writes novels at home. でもある adds 小説家 as a second identity alongside 医者.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: でもない does not fit this context: the next line says he writes novels on his days off, so denying that he is a novelist contradicts it.

options.label: でもある
options.rationale: My father is a doctor and also a novelist. On his days off he writes novels at home. でもある adds 小説家 as a second identity alongside 医者.

exercises.prompt: この店の料理は安い。しかも、体にいい料理____。
exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: しかも adds a further good point to the first one.
exercises.explanation: The food at this restaurant is cheap. Moreover, it is also good for your health. しかも introduces an added merit, and でもある states it as a further quality of the same food.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: でもない does not fit this context: しかも introduces an additional point in the same direction, and a denial would not continue the praise.

options.label: でもある
options.rationale: The food at this restaurant is cheap. Moreover, it is also good for your health. しかも introduces an added merit, and でもある states it as a further quality of the same food.

exercises.prompt: 彼は私の上司だが、休みの日には一緒に釣りに行く友人____。
exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The clause before 友人 says they go fishing together, so he is a friend as well as a boss.
exercises.explanation: He is my boss, but he is also a friend I go fishing with on days off. だが contrasts the work role with a private one, and でもある adds that second identity.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: でもない does not fit this context: the modifier says they go fishing together on days off, which describes the friend he is; denying it contradicts the clause.

options.label: でもある
options.rationale: He is my boss, but he is also a friend I go fishing with on days off. だが contrasts the work role with a private one, and でもある adds that second identity.

exercises.prompt:
この仕事は楽ではないが、やりがいのある仕事____。
毎日新しいことを学べるので、楽しい。
exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The next line says you learn new things every day and enjoy it.
exercises.explanation: This job is not easy, but it is also a rewarding job. I can learn new things every day, so it is enjoyable. でもある adds a positive quality after the negative 楽ではない; the next line supports 'rewarding'.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: でもない does not fit this context: the next line says you learn new things every day and enjoy it, so denying that the job is rewarding contradicts it.

options.label: でもある
options.rationale: This job is not easy, but it is also a rewarding job. I can learn new things every day, so it is enjoyable. でもある adds a positive quality after the negative 楽ではない; the next line supports 'rewarding'.

exercises.prompt:
この仕事は楽ではないが、特に難しい仕事____。
一週間で慣れるだろう。
exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The next line says one week is enough to get used to it, so the job is not especially hard.
exercises.explanation: This job is not easy, but it is not especially difficult either. You will probably get used to it in a week. でもない denies a second description after 楽ではない; the next line rules out 'difficult'.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: This job is not easy, but it is not especially difficult either. You will probably get used to it in a week. でもない denies a second description after 楽ではない; the next line rules out 'difficult'.

options.label: でもある
options.rationale: でもある does not fit this context: the next line says you will get used to it in a week, so calling it an especially difficult job as well contradicts it.

exercises.prompt:
彼は歌手ではないし、俳優____。

exercises.translation: Insert only でもある or でもない. Recognized spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The next line says he is an ordinary office worker.
exercises.explanation: He is not a singer, and he is not an actor either. He is an ordinary office worker. でもない adds a second denied identity after 歌手ではない.

options.label: でもない
options.rationale: He is not a singer, and he is not an actor either. He is an ordinary office worker. でもない adds a second denied identity after 歌手ではない.

exercises.prompt: 「当店の定休日は、水曜日となっております。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: A shop informs customers of its regular closing day.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: Our regular closing day is Wednesday. となっております politely states an arrangement that is in effect; the sentence describes no earlier state.

options.label: 変化
options.rationale: 変化 does not fit this sentence: nothing contrasts an earlier state with a new one; the shop informs customers of its regular closing day.

options.label: 決まり
options.rationale: The sentence means: Our regular closing day is Wednesday. となっております politely states an arrangement that is in effect; the sentence describes no earlier state.

exercises.prompt: 「会議室の利用は、一回二時間までとなっています。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: まで sets a limit on how long the room may be used.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: Use of the meeting room is limited to two hours at a time. となっています states a rule that applies to users.

options.label: 変化
options.rationale: 変化 does not fit this sentence: it sets a time limit for users and mentions no earlier situation that changed.

options.label: 決まり
options.rationale: The sentence means: Use of the meeting room is limited to two hours at a time. となっています states a rule that applies to users.

exercises.prompt: 「この公園でのボール遊びは禁止となっています。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 禁止 names something that users of the park are not allowed to do.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: Ball games are prohibited in this park. となっています presents the prohibition as a rule in effect.

options.label: 変化

options.label: 決まり
options.rationale: The sentence means: Ball games are prohibited in this park. となっています presents the prohibition as a rule in effect.

exercises.prompt: 「規則では、入場は十八歳以上となっている。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 規則では names the source: the sentence reports what the regulations say.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: According to the regulations, admission is for those aged eighteen and over. となっている states a condition that is in effect; the sentence describes no earlier state.

options.label: 変化
options.rationale: 変化 does not fit this sentence: 規則では introduces what the regulations set, and nothing contrasts an earlier state with a new one.

options.label: 決まり
options.rationale: The sentence means: According to the regulations, admission is for those aged eighteen and over. となっている states a condition that is in effect; the sentence describes no earlier state.

exercises.prompt: 「十年前は静かな村だったが、今では人気の観光地となっている。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.

exercises.explanation: The sentence means: Ten years ago it was a quiet village, but now it has become a popular tourist spot. となっている describes the state the place has reached through change.

exercises.prompt: 「値段が下がった結果、パソコンは生活に欠かせない道具となっている。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and type the sense of its となっている／となっております: 決まり（きまり, a rule or fixed arrangement that is in effect）or 変化（へんか, a state that the subject has come to be in through change）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 値段が下がった結果 names an event that led to the present state.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: As a result of falling prices, personal computers have become indispensable tools in daily life. となっている describes the state reached as a result of that change.

options.label: 変化
options.rationale: The sentence means: As a result of falling prices, personal computers have become indispensable tools in daily life. となっている describes the state reached as a result of that change.

options.label: 決まり
options.rationale: 決まり does not fit this sentence: 結果 presents the state as the outcome of prices falling; nobody set a rule.

exercises.prompt: まず手を____、それから料理を始める。
exercises.translation: Base: 洗う（あらう）, wash. Write the written-style link that goes before the comma: the bare stem (連用形, for example 読む → 読み) if the action takes place, or the ず form (読む → 読まず) if it does not. Do not use a て-form. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: まず … それから presents washing as the first of two steps.
exercises.explanation: First wash your hands, then start cooking. まず and それから present two actions in order, so washing takes place: the stem 洗い links the first clause in written style.

options.label: 洗い
options.rationale: First wash your hands, then start cooking. まず and それから present two actions in order, so washing takes place: the stem 洗い links the first clause in written style.

options.label: 洗わず
options.rationale: 洗わず does not fit this context: まず … それから lists washing as the first step that is done.

exercises.prompt: 駅で友人と____、一緒に会場へ向かった。
exercises.translation: Base: 会う（あう）, meet. Write the written-style link that goes before the comma: the bare stem (連用形, for example 読む → 読み) if the action takes place, or the ず form (読む → 読まず) if it does not. Do not use a て-form. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 一緒に in the next clause shows that the two people met.
exercises.explanation: I met my friend at the station, and we headed to the venue together. 一緒に shows that the meeting took place, so the stem 会い links the clauses.

options.label: 会い
options.rationale: I met my friend at the station, and we headed to the venue together. 一緒に shows that the meeting took place, so the stem 会い links the clauses.

options.label: 会わず
options.rationale: 会わず does not fit this context: the next clause says they went to the venue together, so they did meet.

exercises.prompt: 毎日三十分____、少しずつ体力をつけた。
exercises.translation: Base: 運動する（うんどうする）, exercise. Write the written-style link that goes before the comma: the bare stem (連用形, for example 読む → 読み) if the action takes place, or the ず form (読む → 読まず) if it does not. Do not use a て-form. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The second clause says stamina was built up, which follows from exercising.
exercises.explanation: I exercised for thirty minutes every day and gradually built up my stamina. The stem of 運動する is 運動し, which links the clauses in written style.

options.label: 運動し
options.rationale: I exercised for thirty minutes every day and gradually built up my stamina. The stem of 運動する is 運動し, which links the clauses in written style.

options.label: 運動せず
options.rationale: 運動せず does not fit this context: the second clause says stamina was gradually built up, which follows from exercising every day.

exercises.prompt: 彼は何も____、部屋を出ていった。
exercises.translation: Base: 言う（いう）, say. Write the written-style link that goes before the comma: the bare stem (連用形, for example 読む → 読み) if the action takes place, or the ず form (読む → 読まず) if it does not. Do not use a て-form. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 何も before the verb calls for a negative.
exercises.explanation: He left the room without saying anything. 何も needs a negative verb, so the written negative link 言わず is required; 言わずに is also accepted.

options.label: 言い
options.rationale: 言い does not fit this context: 何も before the blank needs a negative verb, and 言い is affirmative.

options.label: 言わず
options.rationale: He left the room without saying anything. 何も needs a negative verb, so the written negative link 言わず is required; 言わずに is also accepted.

exercises.prompt: 一度も____、最後まで走った。
exercises.translation: Base: 休憩する（きゅうけいする）, take a break. Write the written-style link that goes before the comma: the bare stem (連用形, for example 読む → 読み) if the action takes place, or the ず form (読む → 読まず) if it does not. Do not use a て-form. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 一度も before the verb calls for a negative.
exercises.explanation: I ran to the end without taking a single break. 一度も needs a negative verb; the written negative of 休憩する is 休憩せず (する → せず). 休憩せずに is also accepted.

options.label: 休憩し
options.rationale: 休憩し does not fit this context: 一度も before the blank needs a negative verb, and 休憩し is affirmative.

options.label: 休憩せず
options.rationale: I ran to the end without taking a single break. 一度も needs a negative verb; the written negative of 休憩する is 休憩せず (する → せず). 休憩せずに is also accepted.

exercises.prompt:
辞書を使わないで読んだ。
→辞書を____読んだ。
exercises.translation: The first line uses one 'without' form: ないで or ずに. Rewrite that verb in the other form on the second line (ないで → ずに, ずに → ないで) and keep everything else. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The first line has ないで, so the rewrite needs ずに.
exercises.explanation: I read it without using a dictionary. ない-form 使わない minus ない gives 使わ; add ずに: 使わずに. 使わず alone is also accepted.

options.label: 使わずに
options.rationale: I read it without using a dictionary. ない-form 使わない minus ない gives 使わ; add ずに: 使わずに. 使わず alone is also accepted.

options.label: 使わないで
options.rationale: 使わないで does not fit this task: it repeats the form already given on the first line, and the task asks for the other form.

exercises.translation: The first line uses one 'without' form: ないで or ずに. Rewrite that verb in the other form on the second line (ないで → ずに, ずに → ないで) and keep everything else. Kana and kanji spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The first line has ないで, so the rewrite needs ずに; する becomes せ.
exercises.explanation: I decided without consulting anyone. する verbs take せずに: 相談しないで → 相談せずに. 相談せず alone is also accepted.

options.label: 相談せずに
options.rationale: I decided without consulting anyone. する verbs take せずに: 相談しないで → 相談せずに. 相談せず alone is also accepted.

options.label: 相談しないで

options.label: 予約しないで

exercises.prompt: 「この店には、予約なしでは入れません。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say whether the thing before なし is needed for what the sentence describes: 必要（ひつよう, needed）or 不要（ふよう, not needed）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: なしでは is followed by a negative: without a reservation, entry is impossible.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: You cannot enter this restaurant without a reservation. なしでは + a negative says the reservation is required.

options.label: 必要
options.rationale: The sentence means: You cannot enter this restaurant without a reservation. なしでは + a negative says the reservation is required.

options.label: 不要
options.rationale: 不要 does not fit this sentence: なしでは is followed by 入れません, so without a reservation you cannot get in.

exercises.prompt: 「この仕事は、英語なしではできない。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say whether the thing before なし is needed for what the sentence describes: 必要（ひつよう, needed）or 不要（ふよう, not needed）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: なしでは is followed by a negative: without English, the job cannot be done.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: This job cannot be done without English. なしでは + できない marks English as required.

options.label: 必要
options.rationale: The sentence means: This job cannot be done without English. なしでは + できない marks English as required.

options.label: 不要
options.rationale: 不要 does not fit this sentence: なしでは is followed by できない, so the job is impossible without English.

exercises.prompt: 「この店には、予約なしでも入れます。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say whether the thing before なし is needed for what the sentence describes: 必要（ひつよう, needed）or 不要（ふよう, not needed）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: なしでも is followed by an affirmative: even without a reservation, entry is possible.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: You can enter this restaurant even without a reservation. なしでも + an affirmative says the reservation is not required.

options.label: 必要
options.rationale: 必要 does not fit this sentence: なしでも is followed by 入れます, so you can get in without a reservation.

options.label: 不要
options.rationale: The sentence means: You can enter this restaurant even without a reservation. なしでも + an affirmative says the reservation is not required.

exercises.prompt: 「私はいつも砂糖なしでコーヒーを飲む。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say whether the thing before なし is needed for what the sentence describes: 必要（ひつよう, needed）or 不要（ふよう, not needed）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: なしで describes the speaker's usual way of drinking coffee.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: I always drink my coffee without sugar. Noun + なしで describes how the action is done; sugar is not needed.

options.label: 必要
options.rationale: 必要 does not fit this sentence: the speaker always drinks coffee without sugar, so sugar is not needed for it.

options.label: 不要
options.rationale: The sentence means: I always drink my coffee without sugar. Noun + なしで describes how the action is done; sugar is not needed.

exercises.prompt: 「合格の知らせを聞いて、どんなにうれしかったことか。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say what it does with the amount or degree: 強調（きょうちょう, the speaker exclaims how great it was）or 質問（しつもん, the amount is not known and someone asks about it）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: どんなに … ことか ends the sentence with no listener being asked anything.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: How happy I was when I heard I had passed! どんなに … ことか exclaims the great degree of joy; nobody is asked for an answer.

options.label: 強調
options.rationale: The sentence means: How happy I was when I heard I had passed! どんなに … ことか exclaims the great degree of joy; nobody is asked for an answer.

options.label: 質問
options.rationale: 質問 does not fit this sentence: どんなに … ことか ends the sentence as the speaker's own exclamation, and no one is asked how happy the speaker was.

exercises.prompt: 「この日を何年待ったことか。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say what it does with the amount or degree: 強調（きょうちょう, the speaker exclaims how great it was）or 質問（しつもん, the amount is not known and someone asks about it）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: 何年 … ことか closes the sentence as the speaker's own exclamation.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: How many years I have waited for this day! 何年 … ことか stresses how long the wait was; the speaker is not asking for the number of years.

options.label: 強調
options.rationale: The sentence means: How many years I have waited for this day! 何年 … ことか stresses how long the wait was; the speaker is not asking for the number of years.

options.label: 質問
options.rationale: 質問 does not fit this sentence: 何年 … ことか is the speaker's exclamation about a long wait, and no one is asked to give the number.

exercises.prompt: 「あの時の先生の言葉にどれほど助けられたことか。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say what it does with the amount or degree: 強調（きょうちょう, the speaker exclaims how great it was）or 質問（しつもん, the amount is not known and someone asks about it）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: どれほど … ことか closes the sentence as the speaker's own exclamation.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: How much my teacher's words helped me back then! どれほど … ことか stresses the great degree of help.

options.label: 強調
options.rationale: The sentence means: How much my teacher's words helped me back then! どれほど … ことか stresses the great degree of help.

options.label: 質問
options.rationale: 質問 does not fit this sentence: どれほど … ことか is the speaker's exclamation, and no one is asked how much the words helped.

exercises.prompt: 「駅までどれくらいかかるか、教えてください。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say what it does with the amount or degree: 強調（きょうちょう, the speaker exclaims how great it was）or 質問（しつもん, the amount is not known and someone asks about it）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The か clause is the object of 教えてください: the speaker asks for the travel time.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: Please tell me how long it takes to the station. The embedded question with か asks for an amount the speaker does not know.

options.label: 強調
options.rationale: 強調 does not fit this sentence: the か clause is followed by 教えてください, so the speaker is asking for the time, not exclaiming about it.

options.label: 質問
options.rationale: The sentence means: Please tell me how long it takes to the station. The embedded question with か asks for an amount the speaker does not know.

exercises.prompt: 「何年待ったか、友達に聞かれた。」→____
exercises.translation: Read the Japanese sentence and say what it does with the amount or degree: 強調（きょうちょう, the speaker exclaims how great it was）or 質問（しつもん, the amount is not known and someone asks about it）. Kana spellings are accepted.
exercises.evidence: The か clause is what the friend asked: the number of years was asked about.
exercises.explanation: The sentence means: A friend asked me how many years I had waited. The embedded question with か reports what was asked.

options.rationale: 強調 does not fit this sentence: the か clause is followed by 友達に聞かれた, so it reports a question the friend asked.

options.label: 質問
options.rationale: The sentence means: A friend asked me how many years I had waited. The embedded question with か reports what was asked.
